introduction.en: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations established by the 1944 Chicago Convention to manage the administration and governance of the Convention on International Civil Aviation.
introduction.hi: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations established by the 1944 Chicago Convention to manage the administration and governance of the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

body.en: ICAO plays a pivotal role by setting Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs) which form the basis for global aviation safety. Through the Universal Safety Oversight Audit Programme (USOAP), it monitors the safety oversight capabilities of member states. For India, adherence to ICAO standards is mandatory for international operations. It ensures that Indian carriers meet global safety benchmarks, which is crucial for maintaining the country's safety rating by bodies like the FAA.

conclusion.en: ICAO acts as the backbone of global air connectivity. By harmonizing regulations, it ensures that aviation remains a safe, secure, and sustainable mode of transport for India and the world.
